r0.why: Real-valued f, support = non-zero inputs [1], smallest set with f zero outside [5], used widely in analysis [3].

r1.why: Topology as extra structure [6], smallest closed set containing non-zero points [2], most common case continuous f on real line or R^n [8].

r2.why: Compact closed support [11], equals bounded on R^n since compact iff closed and bounded [12], stronger than vanishing at infinity [15], 1/(1+x^2) example [16].

r3.why: Bump functions [17], mollifiers special case approximating nonsmooth functions [18], dense in many topologies so fundamental [24].

r4.why: Loose closure-of-values picture [33], formal smallest closed set with P=1 [35]; 'certain to land in' paraphrases probability 1.

r5.why: Essential support depends on measure and may be smaller [26], Dirichlet example with Lebesgue measure [27], analysts nearly always prefer it when different [28].
